facts.text: Lake Louise is 186 km west of Calgary and 56 km northwest of Banff on Highway 1.
An alternative from Banff is the Bow Valley Parkway (Highway 1A), a narrower tree-lined road with a better chance of seeing wildlife such as bears and deer.
Calgary International Airport is a 2½-hour drive to Lake Louise, and shuttles can drop off at hotels in Banff and Lake Louise.
The Icefields Parkway connects Lake Louise to Jasper and is 230 km (142 mi).
To reach the Lake Louise lakeshore, book the Parks Canada Shuttle in advance, park at the Park and Ride at Lake Louise Ski Resort, and take a bus every 20 minutes.
Private vehicles are forbidden from driving up to Moraine Lake, so you must reserve a shuttle in advance.
facts.quote: Private vehicles are forbidden from driving up to the lake

facts.text: Before 8AM you can see Lake Louise with few people around; just before dusk is also reasonably quiet.
Lake Louise is best seen first thing in the morning before other tourists arrive, or in the early evening after they have gone.
facts.quote: Best seen first thing in the morning

facts.text: At Moraine Lake, coach groups start to arrive by 8:30AM.
facts.quote: By 8:30AM the coach groups start to arrive

facts.text: Parking at Lake Louise costs $36.75 (2025) and fills up before sunrise, remaining full until sunset.
